name: Precipitation / Rainfall
description: Total atmospheric water vapor condensation falling as liquid precipitation over the crop growth window.
importance: Primary natural replenishment mechanism for soil profile moisture, dictating whether rainfed agriculture is viable or supplemental irrigation is required.

precipitation_regimes.drought_stress: < 50 mm (severe moisture deficiency; requires drought-hardy pulses/millets or drip irrigation)
precipitation_regimes.semi_arid: 50 - 100 mm (suitable for dryland pulses, chickpeas, maize with water conservation)
precipitation_regimes.sub_humid: 100 - 200 mm (favorable for cotton, pigeonpeas, groundnut, fruit crops)
precipitation_regimes.humid_pluvial: > 200 mm (suitable for water-intensive crops like paddy rice and jute; creates waterlogging hazard for pulses)

water_management: Construct broad-bed furrows or raised beds in heavy soils experiencing rainfall exceeding 180 mm to prevent root suffocation.
Practice in-situ rainwater harvesting (farm ponds, check dams, contour bunding) in rainfed zones.
Adopt drip irrigation or mulching in low rainfall belts to maximize crop water-use efficiency.
